p.u: Upon entry of this Response, claims 1-16 and 18-20 are pending in the present patent application. Claims 3-5, 6,

13, and 15 are amended. Claims 18-20 are newly added. Claim 17 is cancelled without waiver, prejudice, or disclaimer. Applicant reserves the right to present this cancelled claim, or variants thereof, in continuing applications. Reconsideration of the presently pending claims in view of the following remarks is respectfully requested.

body.p: I. Claims 3-8, 11, 13, and 15-16 Satisfy the Requirements of 35 U.S.C. @ 112(b)

On page 2 of the Office Action, claims 3-8, 11, 13, and 15-17 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the Applicant regards as the invention. Applicant notes that claim 17 has been cancelled, thereby rendering the rejection of claim 17 moot. Applicant respectfully submits that claims 3-8, 11, 13, and 15-16, as amended, satisfy the requirements of the 35 U.S.C. @ 112 (b). Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 3-8, 11, 13, and 15-16 be withdrawn.

p.u: II. Claims 1-16 Are Patentable over the Cited References

body.p: On pages 3-10 of the Office Action, claims 1-4 and 11-16 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by Burrows, et al. (US Pub. 2013/0206907, hereinafter Burrows); claims 5-8 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Burrows in view of Swain (US Pub. 2014/0123571, hereinafter Swain); claim 9 has been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a)

p.u: as allegedly being unpatentable over Burrows in view of Hanay, et al. (US Pat. 6,079,669, hereinafter Hanay); claim 10 has been rejected under 35 U.S.C.
103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Burrows in view of Seibt (WO Pub. 2014/154758, hereinafter Seibt); and claim 17 has been rejected under 35 U.S.C.

103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Hanay. Applicant notes that claim 17 has been cancelled, thereby rendering the rejection of claim 17 moot. For at least the following reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 1-16 be withdrawn.
A. Claims 1-14
To begin, Applicant respectfully submits that Burrows fails to show or suggest each and every element of claim 1. Claim 1 recites:
A lavatory unit for an aircraft cabin,
wherein the lavatory unit is configurable between an able- bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible configuration
wherein in the able-bodied configuration the lavatory unit has a first
internal floor space and there is a cabin floor space external to the lavatory
unit,
wherein the lavatory unit is expandable into the PRM-accessible
configuration in which the lavatory unit is expanded to have a second internal floor space, the second internal floor space encompassing a
region of the cabin floor space.

(Emphasis added). In rejecting claim 1, the Office Action (pp. 3-4) alleges that Burrows discloses each and every element of claim 1. Applicant respectfully disagrees. For example, Applicant respectfully submits that Burrows fails to disclose a lavatory unit that is configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible configuration and the lavatory unit is expandable into the PRM-accessible configuration as required by claim 1.
Page 1 lines 14 to 18 of the P
C

T Application corresponding to the present application sets out the requirements for a lavatory unit to be PRM-accessible, which include being able to accommodate a PRM (Person of Reduced Mobility) in a wheelchair and allow for a transfer of the PRM from the wheelchair to the toilet.

Applicant respectfully submits that Burrows fails to disclose a lavatory unit that is PRM-accessible. Burrows does not explicitly refer to a PRM or PRM accessibility. Nor is this feature inherent in Burrows. For example, there is no disclosure that the opening of the door 26 (see Fig 3/Fig. 3A of Burrows) is suitable for a PRM to enter the lavatory monument assembly 10 in a wheelchair when the unit is expanded or that the floor space in the expanded configuration is suitable for a PRM. At [0036] of Burrows, the lavatory monuments 10 of the Fig. 5 example of are described as being 25" wide. It is not clear whether this is before or after the first wall 16 is moved but, in any event, it is self-evident that the lavatory monuments as shown in Fig. 5 would not be PRM-accessible even if the 25" width refers to the monument prior to movement of the first wall 16. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Burrows fails to show or suggest at least the above- recited elements of amended claim 1.

Furthermore, as regards the other cited art, Applicant respectfully submits that Swain fails to disclose wherein the lavatory unit is configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible configuration and the lavatory unit is expandable into the PRM-accessible configuration in which the lavatory unit is expanded to have a second internal floor space, the second internal floor space encompassing a region of the cabin floor space as required by claim 1.

Swain refers to a two-toilet lavatory unit, which is an arrangement discussed in the background section of the current application (see page 1, line 26 to page 2, line 2). Removal of a partition allows a user to access both areas but the lavatory unit itself does not expand to encompass a cabin floor space that was previously external to the lavatory unit. To the extent Swain discloses a unit that is configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible configuration that unit comprises both of the two toilet areas as the structure of both areas is required to define the internal floor area in the PRM-accessible configuration. The footprint of the two toilet lavatory unit of Swain does not expand and accordingly Swain fails to disclose the lavatory unit is expanded to have a second internal floor space, the second internal floor space encompassing a region of the cabin floor space.
Further, the skilled person would not understand a first one of the toilet areas of Swain to be a
unit'. Even if the first toilet area is construed as a
unit' then that unit is not expanded (does not increase in size) in Swain - is it simply connected to another unit. Thus, Swain fails to remedy the deficiencies of Burrows as regards claim 1.

Seibt discloses a lavatory unit with a transition seating support (see abstract) that allows a user to transfer from a wheelchair to the transition seating support and then from the transition seating support to the lavatory. As per page 6, lines 8 to 20 of Seibt, this allows the lavatory unit can actually be provided rather small, since, for example the wheelchair stays outside the lavatory unit. So, the lavatory unit of Seibt is not PRM accessible because it cannot accommodate a PRM in a wheelchair. Further, Seibt does not suggest expanding the lavatory unit. Accordingly, Seibt fails to disclose wherein the lavatory unit is configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible
configuration and the lavatory unit is expandable into the PRM-accessible configuration as required by claim 1. Thus, Seibt fails to remedy the deficiencies of Burrows as regards claim 1.

Hanay fails to disclose (explicitly or inherently) a lavatory unit that is PRM- accessible. Further, it appears that the lavatory of Hanay is not useable in its stowed position: col. 5 lines 1 to 5 suggest that sufficient shoulder space for an occupant is only provided in an expanded or deployed state. Thus, Hanay fails to disclose a lavatory unit configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible configuration as required by claim 1. Thus, Hanay fails to remedy the deficiencies of Burrows as regards claim 1.

For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references fail to show or suggest each and every element of claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 be withdrawn. In addition, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 2-14 be withdrawn for at least the reason that claims 2-16 depend from claim 1.

Insofar as claim 15 recites elements similar in scope to those of claim 1, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 15 be withdrawn for at least similar reasons, to the extent applicable. In addition, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 16 be withdrawn for at least the reason that claims 16 depends from claim 15.
III. New Claims 18-20

Applicant notes that claims 18-20 are newly added and contain no new matter. Applicant respectfully submits that claims 18-20 are allowable for at least the reason that claims 18-20 depend from claims 1 or 15.
IV. No Waiver

Applicant's arguments and amendments are without prejudice, waiver, or disclaimer. Applicant has not addressed each specific rejection of the dependent claims because Applicant submits that the independent claims are allowable over the documents of record, as discussed above. Applicant has not acquiesced to any such rejection and reserves the right to address the patentability of any additional claim elements in the future.

It is requested that all outstanding objections and rejections be withdrawn and that this application and all presently pending claims be allowed to issue.
